S4_CLOSED_WORLD_CENSUS.rule: CLOSED-WORLD. Every relation in the tenant universe is placed in EXACTLY ONE class. A relation carrying organization_id that is absent from the welded set is a FINDING with an explicit disposition, never a silent omission.
S4_CLOSED_WORLD_CENSUS.partition_completeness_proof: The 42 organization_id relations partition as 34 WELDED_BY_S4 + 5 nullable (SHARED_REFERENCE_NULL_ORG and TENANTLESS_AUDIT_OR_SYSTEM) + 2 EXCLUDED identity substrate (organization_members, invitations) + 1 EXCLUDED owner-only (entitlement_grants) = 42. No remainder. public.organizations is the fifth relation without an organization_id column and is classified under EXCLUDED_WITH_REASON.

WELDED_BY_S4.predicate: organization_id NOT NULL, carrying at least one membership-based policy, and reached ONLY from organization-scoped contexts.

PARENT_SCOPED_TRANSITIVE.finding: These four are tenant-scoped but carry NO organization_id column. Every policy scopes them as project_id IN (SELECT id FROM public.projects WHERE organization_id = ...). A predicate of the form organization_id = current_setting('app.organization_id') is NOT EVEN EXPRESSIBLE on them.
PARENT_SCOPED_TRANSITIVE.hypothesis_that_MUST_NOT_be_assumed: That welding public.projects restrictively transitively scopes these four, because their policy subqueries read projects and would inherit its row-level security.
PARENT_SCOPED_TRANSITIVE.why_it_must_be_proven_not_assumed: Whether a relation referenced inside another relation's policy expression is itself subject to row-level security is a RUNTIME property of PostgreSQL policy evaluation, and it interacts with ownership: public.projects is owned by uellix_owner and does NOT carry FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so an evaluation path running as the owner is exempt from its policies. A transitive weld that holds for one invoking role and not another is not a weld.
PARENT_SCOPED_TRANSITIVE.disposition: The S4 implementing node MUST decide this by Real-PG probe PG-S4-7, not by reading SQL. If transitivity does NOT hold for the invoking role, each of the four requires its OWN restrictive conjunct written against the projects subquery. Either outcome is acceptable; leaving it undetermined is NOT.

membership_conjunct.rule: UNCHANGED. The existing PERMISSIVE membership policies are not edited, not widened and not narrowed by S4.
membership_conjunct.prohibition: The GUC MUST NOT replace the membership proof. A relation authorized by selected-organization equality ALONE moves the tenant boundary out of the database and into application code, which is the failure row-level security exists to prevent.

selected_org_conjunct.rule: NEW. Published as a RESTRICTIVE policy.
selected_org_conjunct.why_restrictive_is_the_correct_mechanism: PostgreSQL combines PERMISSIVE policies with OR and RESTRICTIVE policies with AND, then combines the two groups with AND. A PERMISSIVE selected-organization policy would be satisfied whenever ANY other permissive policy on the relation is satisfied, and every welded relation already has one. It would therefore enforce NOTHING. Only a RESTRICTIVE policy yields a conjunct that cannot be satisfied around.
selected_org_conjunct.prohibition: No disjunctive or permissive widening. A selected-org term written as an additional PERMISSIVE policy is a defect, not a variant.

GUC_CONTRACT.lifetime: TRANSACTION-LOCAL. The third argument true is LOAD-BEARING and MUST be preserved: a session-scoped GUC would leak tenant scope across pooled connections.
GUC_CONTRACT.set_only_when_scoped: MEASURED: the set_config call is guarded by if (identity.organizationId !== null). When a context is opened unscoped the GUC is NOT set to empty — it is never set at all.
GUC_CONTRACT.value_provenance: A validated organization id that has passed REQUEST_REVALIDATION. Never a client-supplied value, never empty, never NULL within a tenant-scoped transaction.
GUC_CONTRACT.absence_behavior: current_setting('app.organization_id', true) returns NULL when unset. A predicate organization_id = current_setting('app.organization_id', true)::uuid then evaluates to NULL, which is not TRUE, which DENIES.
GUC_CONTRACT.two_argument_form_is_mandatory: The implementing node MUST use the two-argument current_setting(name, true) form. The one-argument form RAISES on an unset GUC. Inside can_write_evidence_object and can_read_evidence_object that exception would be swallowed by their existing EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN false handler, making the denial an accident of error handling rather than an intended decision, and making a genuine fault indistinguishable from a correct refusal.
GUC_CONTRACT.fail_closed_requirement: With the GUC unset, a WELDED relation MUST yield zero rows and MUST permit no writes. This MUST be proven by Real-PG control PG-S4-2 and never inferred from the SQL text.

the_fail_closed_rule_is_scoped_not_globa.statement: Fail-closed-on-unset-GUC applies to the 34 WELDED_BY_S4 relations. It MUST NOT be applied to the identity substrate.
the_fail_closed_rule_is_scoped_not_globa.why: See GUC_UNSET_SUBSTRATE. Seven production entry points deliberately open unscoped contexts. Applying the fail-closed weld to the relations those paths read converts a tenant-isolation win into a total product lockout.

GUC_UNSET_SUBSTRATE.statement: A naive application of the parent authority's own fail-closed rule to the identity substrate produces a BOOTSTRAP DEADLOCK: no subject can ever select an organization, because selecting one requires reading relations that the weld would hide until one is already selected.

closed_world_of_GUC_UNSET_ENTRY_POINTS.method: Enumerated from every non-test construction of withDatabaseIdentityContext in the repository, classified by whether it passes organizationId: null.

The S4 implementing node MUST deliver a control that turns RED when an eighth unscoped construction appears, or the property silently decays.

GUC_UNSET_SUBSTRATE.consequence_if_ignored: listSelectableMemberships runs unscoped BY DESIGN — the S3 contract comment at lib/auth/database-context.ts:911-920 states that enumerating candidates must not require having already selected one. If organization_members or organizations is welded fail-closed, that query returns ZERO rows for every subject, the selector renders an empty list, and no organization can ever be chosen.
GUC_UNSET_SUBSTRATE.disposition: The identity substrate (public.organizations, public.organization_members, public.invitations) is EXCLUDED from the S4 weld, explicitly and with a control, not by omission.

NULL_ORGANIZATION_DISPOSITIONS.method: Derived by replaying column nullability across the applied chain, NOT inherited. The predecessor figure of 5 is INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED at this base; it is used because it was re-measured, never because it was inherited.
NULL_ORGANIZATION_DISPOSITIONS.why_organization_id_IS_NULL_encodes_TWO_: In some relations NULL means SHARED — a globally-valid reference row owned by no tenant. In others NULL means TENANTLESS — a row that structurally cannot have an owning tenant. A single uniform rule cannot serve both.

BOTH_BLANKET_FORMS_ARE_PROHIBITED.why_1_fails: NULL = <anything> evaluates to NULL, not TRUE. Every shared reference row and every tenantless audit row becomes invisible. Shared FX rates and proxy sources disappear from every tenant.
BOTH_BLANKET_FORMS_ARE_PROHIBITED.prohibited_form_2: organization_id IS NULL OR organization_id = current_setting('app.organization_id', true)::uuid applied uniformly.
BOTH_BLANKET_FORMS_ARE_PROHIBITED.why_2_fails: It declares, on EVERY welded relation at once, that a NULL organization_id means visible-to-all. On a tenantless security relation that opens a permanent cross-tenant read channel — created by the very node whose purpose is to close them.

PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.null_semantics: SHARED reference. Global exchange rates carry organization_id IS NULL and are legitimately readable by every tenant.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.evidence: The baseline policy fx_rates_select already carries an EXPLICIT shared disjunct of the form auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND organization_id IS NULL. The shared-row concept predates S4 and is not invented by it.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.disposition: WELD WITH AN EXPLICIT SHARED-ROW DISJUNCT, scoped to this relation only. NULL rows remain readable; non-NULL rows are subject to selected-organization equality.
WELD WITH AN EXPLICIT SHARED-ROW DISJUNCT, per-relation. Same shape as fx_rates.
WELD WITH AN EXPLICIT SHARED-ROW DISJUNCT, per-relation.

PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.null_semantics: SHARED reference, inherited from its parent proxy.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.disposition: WELD WITH AN EXPLICIT SHARED-ROW DISJUNCT, per-relation. The implementing node MUST confirm that a version row's shared status agrees with its parent's; a version whose parent is tenant-owned MUST NOT be reachable as shared.

PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.null_semantics: TENANTLESS, NOT shared. db/migrations/0067_tenancy_refusal_audit_insert_policy.sql requires organization_id IS NULL for the tenancy refusal-audit row precisely because no tenant owns it.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.the_worst_timing: The refusal row is written exactly when no organization has been selected — which is exactly when app.organization_id is unset. A weld of prohibited_form_1 would evaluate NULL = NULL and DENY the write, destroying the audit record of the refusal at the only moment it can be produced.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.disposition: DO NOT apply the generic shared-row disjunct. audit_logs requires its OWN disposition in which tenantless rows are WRITABLE from an unscoped context but are NOT granted blanket cross-tenant READ visibility. Read scoping for tenant-owned audit rows and write reachability for tenantless rows MUST be adjudicated separately, per command, not by one predicate.
PER_TABLE_DISPOSITIONS.prohibition: Treating audit_logs as a fifth shared-reference relation is a DEFECT. It is the one relation in this class where IS NULL means 'no owner', not 'every owner'.

NULL_ORGANIZATION_DISPOSITIONS.over_denial_is_invisible_to_negative_con: A negative control proves a forbidden row is DENIED. It cannot detect that a REQUIRED row has also been denied. Each disposition above therefore requires a POSITIVE canary — a shared or tenantless row that MUST remain visible or writable — or the over-denial failure mode is untested by construction.

ORGANIZATIONS_SELECTOR_DISPOSITION.measured_mechanism: lib/auth/database-context.ts:395 loadSelectableMembershipsWithinContext selects the subject's active rows from organization_members, then loops and calls loadOrganizationWithinContext(row.organizationId) ONCE PER CANDIDATE, and executes if (!organization) continue — silently DISCARDING any candidate whose organizations row it cannot read.
ORGANIZATIONS_SELECTOR_DISPOSITION.failure_is_silent_and_green: The discard path throws nothing and logs nothing. A subject simply sees a shorter list. No existing test can observe the difference, because user_single_active_membership still ceilings every subject to ONE active membership, so a two-candidate fixture cannot be built at this base.
ORGANIZATIONS_SELECTOR_DISPOSITION.strengthening_beyond_the_candidate_findi: The abandoned candidate located the hazard only in public.organizations and predicted a collapse to at most one row. Fresh measurement shows it is worse in two ways. First, the enumerator's FIRST query reads public.organization_members, so welding THAT relation empties the candidate list one step earlier and the organizations loop never runs at all. Second, listSelectableMemberships opens its context with organizationId: null (lib/auth/database-context.ts:933), so the GUC is UNSET during enumeration — the collapse is therefore not to one row but to ZERO rows, for every subject, including a subject with exactly one membership. The result is not a degraded selector; it is a total lockout in which no subject can ever select an organization.

disposition.rule: public.organizations and public.organization_members are EXCLUDED from the S4 restrictive weld. The exclusion is EXPLICIT and carries a control; it is not an omission.
disposition.what_preserves_tenant_safety_instead: Both relations remain governed by their existing membership-scoped PERMISSIVE policies, which already restrict a subject to rows for organizations it belongs to. Excluding them from the SELECTED-org weld does not make them world-readable; it declines to add a SECOND, selection-based conjunct to relations whose entire purpose is to be readable BEFORE a selection exists.
disposition.prohibited_resolution: Solving this by weakening organizations-row security generally — for example by making the relation readable to any authenticated subject — is PROHIBITED. The fix is a scoped exclusion of the selection conjunct, never a relaxation of the membership conjunct.

ORGANIZATIONS_SELECTOR_DISPOSITION.required_control: PG-S4-4 enumerator integrity, under Real PostgreSQL, with a DUAL-MEMBER subject: after S4 is applied, the enumerator must still return BOTH candidates while running with the GUC unset. Because the dual-member fixture is unbuildable while user_single_active_membership exists, this control REQUIRES the two-phase disposable harness described in the companion manifest.

detail: insert_evidence ON storage.objects FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'uellix-evidence' AND public.can_write_evidence_object(name, auth.uid()))
delete_evidence ON storage.objects FOR DELETE TO authenticated USING (bucket_id = 'uellix-evidence' AND public.can_write_evidence_object(name, auth.uid()))
select_evidence ON storage.objects FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (bucket_id = 'uellix-evidence' AND public.can_read_evidence_object(name, auth.uid()))

the_live_gap.statement: public.can_write_evidence_object(object_name text, user_id uuid) authorizes on MEMBERSHIP ALONE and never consults app.organization_id.
the_live_gap.measured_body: db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:892-928. It extracts the project id from the object path, then tests EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.projects p JOIN public.organization_members om ON om.organization_id = p.organization_id WHERE p.id::text = <path segment> AND om.user_id = <caller> AND om.status = 'active' AND om.role IN ('organization_admin','analyst')).
the_live_gap.consequence: A subject who is an active organization_admin or analyst of BOTH organization A and organization B, with organization A selected, may write an evidence object into a project owned by organization B. The selected organization is never consulted. This is exactly the cross-tenant write S4 exists to close, and it becomes reachable the moment S7 permits a second membership.

why_a_table_level_weld_CANNOT_fix_it.measured: can_write_evidence_object is SECURITY DEFINER and ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO uellix_owner. uellix_owner is NOBYPASSRLS (db/baseline/stella_g2_roles.sql:98) but it OWNS public.projects and public.organization_members, and NEITHER relation carries FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — the applied chain FORCEs exactly 4 relations (commercial_accounts, account_legal_acceptances, organization_commercial_acceptances, entitlement_grants), none of them these two.
why_a_table_level_weld_CANNOT_fix_it.conclusion: A relation owner is exempt from its own relation's row-level security unless FORCE is set. The helper's inner join therefore reads past ANY restrictive policy S4 adds to projects or organization_members. The weld CANNOT be inherited; it MUST be written into the helper body.
why_a_table_level_weld_CANNOT_fix_it.NOBYPASSRLS_is_not_the_relevant_property: Reasoning from the role attribute alone would conclude, wrongly, that the helper is already constrained. Ownership plus absent FORCE is what decides it.

frozen_requirement.R1: S4 MUST make the selected organization load-bearing in the governed storage write path, so that a dual-member subject cannot write an object belonging to a non-selected organization.
frozen_requirement.R2: The helper MUST read the CALLER's app.organization_id using the two-argument current_setting form. That the caller's transaction-local GUC is visible INSIDE a SECURITY DEFINER body is a runtime property of PostgreSQL — SECURITY DEFINER changes the effective user, not the transaction's GUC state, and SET search_path TO '' pins only search_path — but it MUST be PROVEN by PG-S4-3 and never assumed.
frozen_requirement.R3: SIGNATURE STABILITY IS MANDATORY. can_write_evidence_object(text, uuid) and can_read_evidence_object(text, uuid) MUST be modified by CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, preserving both signatures exactly. Changing a signature creates a NEW function with default privileges, leaves the old one in place still referenced by the three policies, and silently converts an RLS change into an ACL change. See ACL_INTERACTION.
frozen_requirement.R4: The existing EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RETURN false handler MUST NOT be relied upon to produce the denial. The unset-GUC case MUST be an explicit, intentional branch. A refusal produced by an exception swallow is indistinguishable from a genuine fault and cannot be audited.
frozen_requirement.R5: This authority does NOT modify the storage implementation. It freezes the requirement only.

STORAGE_WELD_CONTRACT.not_absorbed: can_read_evidence_object is named here as in-scope for the same weld, but its body is NOT re-derived in this artifact. The implementing node MUST measure it independently rather than assuming symmetry with the write helper. Recorded as open finding F-S4-9.

SUPERADMIN_COMPATIBILITY.rule: S4 MUST preserve pre-S4 superadmin reach EXACTLY, byte-for-byte in observable behavior, until S5 owns its removal.
SUPERADMIN_COMPATIBILITY.the_trap: S4 can satisfy the parent authority's literal instruction — do not alter the existing OR current_user_is_super_admin() disjuncts — while destroying superadmin reach entirely, because a RESTRICTIVE policy ANDs against the whole permissive group including that disjunct. Textual non-alteration and semantic non-alteration are DIFFERENT properties here, and only the second one matters.
SUPERADMIN_COMPATIBILITY.frozen_compatibility_rule: S4's restrictive conjunct MUST itself carry a superadmin escape, so that the conjunct is satisfied for a superadmin regardless of the selected-organization term. The permissive disjuncts are left untouched, and the restrictive conjunct is written so that it cannot revoke what they grant.
SUPERADMIN_COMPATIBILITY.why_omitting_the_escape_is_NOT_merely_st: Omitting it is an UNANNOUNCED PARTIAL S5 executed inside S4's grant. It changes the superadmin boundary — the thing S5 exists to decide — in a node whose grant does not cover it, and it does so with no diff on any superadmin-related line, making the change invisible to review.
preserved_unchanged_by_S4: The superadmin exemption in db/identity-context.ts:217 (identity.organizationId !== null && check.is_member !== true && !check.is_super_admin).
Policy-level superadmin semantics — all 131 effective policies carrying current_user_is_super_admin.

S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.finding_id: F-AU-1 (re-derived; the predecessor's figures are DISCARDED)
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.decision: S4 MUST PRECEDE S5. This is a HARD DEPENDENCY, not a sequencing preference.
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.postgresql_composition_premise: Row visibility = (OR over PERMISSIVE policies) AND (AND over RESTRICTIVE policies). A restrictive policy is a GLOBAL conjunct over the relation: it constrains every permissive disjunct simultaneously, including ones it does not name.
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.predecessor_figures_discarded: The abandoned candidate measured 95 of 95 across 36 tables, from db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql ALONE. That measurement is superseded: it omits db/migrations/**, which both adds policies and drops baseline ones. The re-derived figure is 125 of 127 across 45 relations.
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.why_the_two_exceptions_do_NOT_weaken_the: Both uncoupled policies sit on ONE relation, added by a migration that landed after the candidate's measurement. 125 of the 127 membership policies still cannot be welded without deciding S5's question, so no ordering other than S4 -> S5 is available for the welded set as a whole.
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.the_ordering_argument: Because S4 must preserve superadmin reach inside its OWN restrictive conjunct (SUPERADMIN_COMPATIBILITY), the superadmin escape becomes part of S4's frozen output. S5 then removes superadmin reach from a surface that is already conjunctively welded, and its diff is auditable as a boundary change alone. Running S5 first would force S4 to weld against a superadmin surface that is concurrently moving, and neither node's effect would be separately provable.
S4_TO_S5_ORDERING.prohibition: S4 and S5 MUST NOT be implemented in one node, and S5 MUST NOT be implemented before S4.

ACL_INTERACTION.symbolic_conclusion: S4 requires an ACL COMPATIBILITY PROOF, not an ACL SUCCESSOR — CONDITIONAL on the two constraints below. If either is violated the conclusion INVERTS and an ACL successor becomes mandatory.

conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.condition: S4 introduces a NEW SQL function — for example a selected-organization accessor helper — used inside a policy expression.
conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.why: Evaluating a policy requires the INVOKING role to hold EXECUTE on every function the expression calls; without it a SELECT by uellix_app does not return zero rows, it fails outright with 42501. A new function would therefore require new EXECUTE grants to uellix_writer and uellix_auditor, and would break the ACL authority's REQUIRED_EXECUTE_POSTURE of EXACTLY three signatures (public.current_user_org_ids(), public.current_user_is_super_admin(), public.current_user_role_in_org(uuid)).
conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.mitigation_that_keeps_S4_ACL_neutral: Write the selected-organization term with the built-in current_setting('app.organization_id', true), which needs no EXECUTE grant, and reuse only the three already-granted helpers.

conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.condition: S4 changes the signature of can_write_evidence_object or can_read_evidence_object.
conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.why: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION on an unchanged signature PRESERVES the existing ACL. A signature change creates a new function carrying default privileges and leaves the old one in place, converting an RLS change into an ACL change silently.
conditions_that_would_force_an_ACL_succe.mitigation: STORAGE_WELD_CONTRACT.R3 already freezes signature stability as mandatory.

ACL_INTERACTION.obligation_on_the_implementing_node: State which branch of the conditional it took, and prove it — an ACL compatibility proof is only valid alongside evidence that no new function was introduced and no signature changed.

REAL_PG_CONTRACT.principle: NO STATIC SQL INSPECTION MAY SUBSTITUTE FOR POSTGRESQL SEMANTICS. Policy combination, definer GUC visibility, NULL-is-not-TRUE denial, owner RLS exemption and transitive policy evaluation are ALL runtime properties.
REAL_PG_CONTRACT.harness: Disposable cluster only, via pnpm db:audit:disposable. NEVER staging, NEVER production, NEVER the canonical local stack.
REAL_PG_CONTRACT.fixture_shape: TWO-TENANT with REAL ROWS in the non-selected organization. A probe returning zero rows merely for want of data proves nothing.
REAL_PG_CONTRACT.two_phase_construction_is_forced: The dual-member subject required by PG-S4-1 and PG-S4-4 is unbuildable while user_single_active_membership exists. It may be constructed ONLY inside a post-S7 phase WITHIN the disposable cluster. Dropping the index early anywhere else is prohibited by DROP_LAST_RULE.prohibited_shortcuts.

probes.requirement: Dual-member subject, selected organization A: a row of A is visible and writable, a row of B is DENIED. Then symmetrically with B selected: a row of B is visible and writable, a row of A is DENIED.
probes.why_runtime: It proves the RESTRICTIVE conjunct actually ANDs against the permissive membership disjunct, which text cannot show.

probes.requirement: With app.organization_id UNSET, a WELDED relation yields ZERO tenant rows and permits ZERO tenant writes.
probes.scope_limit: Applies to the 34 WELDED_BY_S4 relations ONLY. Asserting it over the identity substrate would encode the bootstrap deadlock as a requirement.

probes.requirement: current_setting('app.organization_id', true) observed INSIDE the governed SECURITY DEFINER storage helper resolves to the CALLER's transaction-local value, and a dual-member subject selected on A cannot write an object for a project of B.
probes.why_runtime: SECURITY DEFINER changes the effective user, not the transaction's GUC state — a claim that must be demonstrated, not asserted.

probes.requirement: ENUMERATOR INTEGRITY. After S4, a dual-member subject running the selector with the GUC UNSET still enumerates BOTH selectable organizations.
probes.why_it_is_the_load_bearing_control: This is the single control that would have caught the bootstrap deadlock. It must run with the GUC unset, because that is how the enumerator actually runs in production.

probes.requirement: CLOSED-WORLD CENSUS. An organization-scoped relation that is in NEITHER the welded set NOR the explicit disposition set causes RED.
probes.derivation_rule: The census universe MUST be derived independently from the applied chain, NEVER read from the S4 package under test. A test whose expectation comes from the artifact it checks is vacuous.

probes.requirement: Shared NULL-organization reference data remains visible EXACTLY according to its per-relation disposition: shared rows of fx_rates, proxy_sources, financial_proxies and financial_proxy_versions remain readable, and the tenantless audit_logs refusal row remains WRITABLE from an unscoped context, while no tenant-owned row of any of the five leaks cross-tenant.
probes.why_a_positive_canary_is_mandatory: Negative controls cannot detect over-denial. Without a row that MUST remain visible, a weld that hides all shared data passes every forbidden-access test.

probes.requirement: PARENT-SCOPED TRANSITIVITY. Determine, under the ACTUAL invoking role, whether a restrictive weld on public.projects transitively scopes impact_narratives, indicators, outcomes and stakeholder_groups through their project_id subqueries.
probes.both_outcomes_are_acceptable: If transitivity HOLDS, the four need no direct conjunct but this probe becomes their standing proof. If it does NOT hold, each requires its own conjunct. Leaving it undetermined is NOT acceptable, because the four carry no organization_id column and would otherwise fall outside the census silently.

MUTATION_CONTRACT.principle: Each mutation below MUST turn the suite RED. A mutation that leaves it green means the corresponding guarantee is untested, regardless of how many tests pass.

mutations.mutation: Change the selected-organization policy from RESTRICTIVE to PERMISSIVE.
mutations.why: A permissive selected-org term enforces nothing, because every welded relation already carries a satisfiable permissive membership policy.

mutations.mutation: Remove the membership conjunct, leaving selected-organization equality alone.
mutations.why: It would move the tenant boundary from the database into application code.

mutations.mutation: Remove the selected-organization conjunct, leaving membership alone.
mutations.why: This is the pre-S4 state; if it stays green, S4 proved nothing.

Add public.organizations or public.organization_members to the welded set.
mutations.must: RED via the enumerator-integrity control PG-S4-4, NOT merely via a census count.

mutations.mutation: Reclassify public.audit_logs as a shared-reference relation, applying the generic IS NULL OR equality disjunct to it.
mutations.why: It would grant blanket cross-tenant read visibility to a tenantless security relation.

mutations.mutation: Remove one relation from the closed-world census enumeration.
Add a new organization_id-carrying fixture relation to the universe without classifying it.

Drop the superadmin escape from S4's restrictive conjunct.
mutations.why: This is the unannounced-partial-S5 failure. Without this control the most likely S4 defect is invisible.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: Applying the parent authority's fail-closed rule to the identity substrate produces a total bootstrap deadlock: the enumerator runs with app.organization_id deliberately unset, so a fail-closed weld on organizations or organization_members returns ZERO candidates and no subject can ever select an organization.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED BY THIS ARTIFACT. The substrate is explicitly excluded, and PG-S4-4 is the control that keeps the exclusion honest.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The parent authority's claim that S4 and S5 are independent is measured false at 125 of 127 membership policies across 45 relations.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED BY THIS ARTIFACT. S4 carries the superadmin escape in its own restrictive conjunct; S4 -> S5 is frozen as a hard ordering.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: organization_id IS NULL encodes two incompatible meanings, and BOTH uniform predicates are unsafe.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED BY THIS ARTIFACT via five per-relation dispositions plus mandatory positive canaries.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The governed storage write path authorizes on membership alone and cannot be constrained by any table-level weld, because its SECURITY DEFINER body runs as the owner of two relations that lack FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED AS A FROZEN REQUIREMENT. The weld must be written into the helper body and proven by PG-S4-3. Implementation is NOT performed here.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: Four tenant-scoped relations carry no organization_id column and are scoped only through a projects subquery. Whether a restrictive weld on projects reaches them transitively is undetermined at authority time.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: OPEN BY DESIGN, with a mandatory resolution. PG-S4-7 must decide it; both outcomes are acceptable, silence is not.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: public.entitlement_grants carries organization_id but has no tenant-facing policy at all — its only effective policy is owner-only.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: EXCLUDED WITH REASON, with a standing tripwire: PG-S4-5 forces it back into the welded set if the application role ever gains reach.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The GUC-unset caller set is an ENUMERATION over the repository at one base, not a structural guarantee. A new unscoped construction would silently widen it.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED AS A CONTROL OBLIGATION. M-S4-12 must turn RED on an eighth construction.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: S4 is the FIRST node to publish a restrictive policy into the applied chain; the 18 AS RESTRICTIVE statements that exist live only in unapplied db/prepared units.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RECORDED. S4 establishes the precedent rather than following one. Citing A2-F02 as an applied precedent would be false.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: can_read_evidence_object is in scope for the storage weld but its body was NOT independently re-derived by this authority lane.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: OPEN. The implementing node MUST measure it rather than assuming symmetry with can_write_evidence_object. Declared here so the gap is visible rather than implied.
